title: Cohort-driven prompt harness and adaptive rollback decision framework for Optimize
creator: Aisha Patel
background: Optimize has growing customer adoption for automated model tuning; current eval tooling uses monolithic prompt pools and static thresholds which miss cohort-specific regressions and produce noisy rollback noise. Several customers reported rare but high-severity regressions on tail cohorts (legal/medical phrasing, multi-step instructions). This PRD defines a cohort-aware prompt harness, sampling rules to ensure signal fidelity, and an adaptive rollback decision framework that prioritizes user-impacted cohorts and reduces false positives.
problem_statement: We lack a formalized approach to (1) curate and stratify prompt sets into cohorts that reflect product usage, (2) set statistically-sound regression thresholds per cohort and overall, and (3) execute rollback actions that are proportional to impact. Current rules cause both missed regressions in narrow cohorts and noisy rollbacks from marginal metric drift.
goals: Define deterministic cohort taxonomy (functional, risk, frequency, customer-critical).
Specify sampling matrix for prompt selection that balances head/frequency and adversarial tail coverage.
Formalize per-cohort and global regression thresholds with statistical tests and minimum sample sizes.
Implement a three-tier rollback decision framework (auto-stop, staged rollback, manual review) tied to cohort-weighted impact.
Ship instrumentation and dashboards that show cohort-level signals, sample sizes, and decision rationale in Console.
non_goals: Replacing existing Optimize evaluation engine runtime or full retraining workflows.
Automating corrective model patching or retraining pipelines — this focuses on detection and rollback, not remediation.
Guaranteeing zero false positives for extremely low-volume edge cohorts (we will instead provide manual ops guidance).
scope: In-scope: cohort taxonomy, prompt sampling rules, stat test selection, threshold calibration, rollback action definitions, Console views and alerting. Out-of-scope: model-level fixes, dedicated infra changes beyond light instrumentation, and integrations with external ticketing beyond links to incident/playbooks.
proposed_solution: 1) Cohort taxonomy: Create mutually-exclusive cohorts: Core (top 60% traffic), Functional (by API route/feature), Risk (safety/legal/PII-related), Multistep/Stateful, and Adversarial Tail (rare, hand-curated). 2) Sampling matrix: For each release, sample prompts with stratified weights (Core 60%, Functional 20%, Risk 10%, Multistep 5%, Tail 5% with oversampling rules for Tail prompts). 3) Statistical rules: Use two-sided proportion tests for pass/fail tasks and bootstrap-based confidence intervals for scalar metrics. Require min N per cohort (see acceptance criteria). 4) Thresholds: Define absolute and relative thresholds per cohort with asymmetric tolerances (we allow small positive regressions in low-impact cohorts but strict limits for Risk cohorts). 5) Decision engine: Compute cohort-weighted impact score combining user-facing severity and cohort weight; map scores to three actions: AUTO-STOP (immediate rollback), SCHEDULED-STAGED (progressive traffic reduction + monitoring), MANUAL-REVIEW (alert owners). 6) Console: Expose per-cohort results, sample size, p-values, effect sizes, and decision rationale with a single-click rollback trigger for AUTO-STOP-approved teams.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Cohort taxonomy documented with mapping rules and example prompts for each cohort (published in Confluence).
A2: Sampling harness produces a release-level prompt set matching the stratified weights within +/-5% for Core/Functional buckets and oversamples Tail prompts to reach min N.
A3: Evaluation engine computes cohort metrics and statistical tests within the release window and surfaces p-values, effect sizes, and confidence intervals in Console.
A4: Decision engine produces an explicit action (AUTO-STOP, SCHEDULED-STAGED, MANUAL-REVIEW) and reasoning for all releases; action mapping can be simulated in staging using historical releases.
A5: Rollback actions execute end-to-end in staging (traffic re-route or model pinning) and are reversible.
A6: Dashboards show per-cohort sample sizes, metric deltas, and an audit trail for any automated or manual rollback decisions.
A7: Default thresholds and minimum N are enforced and configurable by PMs; security review completed if Risk cohorts include customer PII scenarios.
metrics: Primary: cohort-weighted regression rate (fraction of cohorts exceeding thresholds), overall pass-rate delta (pre/post).
Secondary: false-positive rollback rate (fraction of rollbacks reversed after manual review), mean time-to-detect, mean time-to-rollback, evaluation cost per release.
User impact proxy: percentage of production traffic affected by AUTO-STOP events
regression_thresholds: Default approach: per-cohort absolute threshold + relative delta. Risk cohorts: absolute decrease in pass-rate >= 1.0 percentage point OR relative degradation >= 5% => high severity. Core cohorts: absolute >= 2.0 pp OR relative >= 7% => medium severity. Tail cohorts: require larger effect sizes and min N before action. Statistical significance: p < 0.01 for AUTO-STOP, p < 0.05 for SCHEDULED-STAGED; use benjamini-hochberg adjustment when testing multiple cohorts to control false discovery rate. Bootstrap intervals for continuous metrics; require overlap tests to guard against low-N noise.
ab_criteria: Minimum sample sizes: detect 3 percentage point absolute change with 80% power at alpha=0.01 => sample sizes computed by harness; fallback rule: if min N not met, mark cohort insufficient and upweight for targeted sampling next release.
Sequential testing: allow early stopping only when cumulative evidence crosses predefined boundaries to avoid peeking errors; use alpha-spending schedule for long-running experiments.
Minimum experiment duration: 72 hours or 50k tokens per variant, whichever comes first, unless AUTO-STOP trigger fires.
rollback_triggers: AUTO-STOP: triggered when Risk cohort severity + cohort-weighted impact score exceeds auto threshold and p < 0.01; immediate rollback of new model variant and notification to SRE/PM.

SCHEDULED-STAGED: triggered when Core cohorts breach medium thresholds or multiple cohorts show correlated drift (p < 0.05); action is staged traffic reduction (50% -> 25% -> 0) with monitoring windows between steps.
MANUAL-REVIEW: triggered when single low-weight cohort breaches threshold but impact score is low; requires PM/owner sign-off within 24 hours to proceed with rollback or mitigation.
monitoring_signals: Per-cohort pass/fail rates and confidence intervals
Effect size and p-values for each metric
Sample sizes and sampling fidelity (expected vs actual weights)
Latency and token-cost delta for the candidate model
Error/backoff rates and user-visible failure metrics
Customer-incident spikes and complaint counts correlated with releases
rollout_plan: 1) Spike: implement cohort taxonomy and sampling harness in staging; run 3 historical release replays to validate signal fidelity.
2) Pilot: enable on Optimize internal releases (alpha customer set) for 2 weeks; exercise manual-review and staged rollback paths.
3) Gradual: enable AUTO-STOP for Risk cohorts only while masking Core AUTO-STOP for 4 weeks; collect metrics and false-positive rates.
4) Full: enable full decision engine with configurable thresholds in Console and training for PM/SE teams.
notes: Trade-offs: stricter thresholds reduce customer-exposed regressions but increase false positives and operational overhead. We bias toward safety for Risk cohorts and toward data-driven leniency for long-tail prompts where sample sizes are small. Open questions: (1) should we include a separate NLU semantic similarity bucketing step for prompt generalization? (2) exact alpha-spending schedule for sequential tests. Action: sync with Applied ML and Stat team next sprint.
